definitions.explanation: The quality of being sticky or adhering to surfaces, or the tendency to cling.

examples.japanese: {粘着性|ねんちゃくせい}のあるテープ。
この{素材|そざい}は{粘着性|ねんちゃくせい}が{高|たか}い。
{温度|おんど}が{上|あ}がると{粘着性|ねんちゃくせい}が{低下|ていか}して、テープが{剥|は}がれやすくなる。
examples.english: When the temperature rises, the adhesiveness decreases and the tape becomes easier to peel off.

notes:
A compound of {粘着|ねんちゃく} (adhesion, sticking) and {性|せい} (quality, property). Used in technical, manufacturing, and everyday contexts to describe the sticky quality of materials like tape, glue, and coatings.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {粘着性|ねんちゃくせい}が{高|たか}い: highly adhesive
- {粘着性|ねんちゃくせい}が{低|ひく}い: low adhesiveness
- {粘着性|ねんちゃくせい}のある: having adhesiveness; sticky
- {粘着性|ねんちゃくせい}を{持|も}つ: to have adhesiveness

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {粘着力|ねんちゃくりょく}: adhesive strength — focuses on the measurable force of adhesion
- {粘性|ねんせい}: viscosity — the resistance of a fluid to flow
- {接着性|せっちゃくせい}: adhesion; bonding quality — the ability to bond two surfaces together
